newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish Riksbank says already eyes unemployment.
newsitem.headline: Swedish Riksbank says already eyes unemployment.

text.p: The governor of Sweden's central bank, Urban Backstrom, said on Thursday that a discussed secondary unemployment target is not a problem as the Riksbank already takes unemployment into account.

"The Maastricht treaty says that monetary policy's price stability target should support general economic policies, which include employment," Backstrom told journalists after a closed meeting with the parliamentary finance committee.

"We will do what we can within the inflation target to support an economic recovery but what we can do is limited by the structural problems we have today," he said. "The Riksbank cannot do anything about that."
The Riksbank's only written target is price stability, to keep inflation at two percent with an allowed deviation of one percentage point on either side.

Daily Dagens Industri reported on Wednesday that the minority Social Democratic government and its informal cooperation partner, the Centre Party, wanted to set secondary central bank targets for unemployment and growth.
"This is a non-discussion, it's old," Backstrom said. "It already exists in the Maastricht treaty."
He added that it was important to clearly write that price stability is the Riksbank's overall target.
